agent_response:

A visit to your GP or primary-care doctor would also be worthwhile — they can do an initial check-up and refer you to a mental-health professional if needed. If you are having thoughts of harming yourself, please reach out to a trusted person or call your local crisis line right away — in the US that is 988, in the UK Samaritans at 116 123. You do not have to go through this alone.

question_text: My cousin has schizophrenia and hears voices. I don't hear voices but I sometimes have dark thoughts. Do I have schizophrenia too? Could it be developing?
agent_response:
I hear how much you want a clear answer, and I would rather be honest that it is not mine to give in either direction. I cannot diagnose or treat any condition — that is a judgment for a clinician who can sit with the whole picture.

An important distinction: dark thoughts (suicidal thoughts, thoughts of being a burden) come from your own mind — they are different from auditory hallucinations, which are heard as voices and can be a symptom of psychosis. Voices heard aloud are a feature of psychosis; dark thoughts of the kind you describe are a different sort of experience. Where your own experience falls is something a clinician can work out with you — that is the conversation worth having, and it is worth having soon.
